title_zh: SEC 试水资产代币化：对话 Janus Henderson 的 Nick Czerny 与 Open Assets 的 Gabor Gurbacs
subtitle_zh: SEC 创新豁免打开代币化证券入美大门，链上将重塑结算与中介，把资本市场向全球更多人敞开。

turns.en: Welcome to ETF EDGE, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange-traded funds, you're in the right place.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 ETF Edge 播客。如果你想了解关于交易所交易基金（ETF）的最新洞见，那你可来对地方了。

turns.en: Every week we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors. I'm your host, Dominic Chu.
turns.zh: 每周我们都会带来精彩的访谈、深入的市场分析，并为大家拆解这一切对投资者意味着什么。我是主持人 Dominic Chu。

turns.en: The SEC has given the nod to tokenization, but there's a catch. And the tokens themselves might not even be the most important part of it. Here's my conversation with Nick Czerny, Giannis Henderson's head of innovation, along with Gabor Gorbache, open assets founder and CEO.
turns.zh: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）已经为代币化（tokenization）开了绿灯，但这里面有个前提。而且代币本身也许还不是其中最关键的部分。以下是我与 Janus Henderson 创新主管 Nick Czerny，以及 Open Assets 创始人兼首席执行官 Gabor Gurbacs 的对话。

turns.en: Thank you both for being here with us right now. Let's talk first of all with a broader question, and I will direct this first towards Nick.
turns.zh: 非常感谢两位现在来到我们节目。我们先从一个更宏观的问题谈起，我想先把这个问题抛给 Nick。

turns.en: I want to know, I have a kind of understanding, but I'm trying to get my arms around tokenization. What exactly does it mean? And what exactly does it mean to have tokenized equities and or ETF products that are going to be coming to market anytime soon?
turns.zh: 我想知道——我大概有个初步的理解，但我还在努力去真正把握代币化到底是什么意思。具体而言，所谓代币化的股票，以及即将很快面市的代币化 ETF 产品，究竟意味着什么？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, eventually what it means is that the broader financial system, whether it's ETFs, mutual funds, your bank accounts, etc., is operating on a new technology stack.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说，从最终层面讲，它意味着整个更广泛的金融体系——不管是 ETF、共同基金（mutual fund），还是你的银行账户等等——都在一套新的技术栈（technology stack）上运行。

turns.en: And that technology stack is blockchain. And today, what's going on there is really around crypto. Most of the activity that's happening on blockchain, people think of it as crypto assets, crypto trading, etc., but eventually we're going to get to a place where it's kind of a lot more boring than that.
turns.zh: 而这整套技术栈就是区块链（blockchain）。今天区块链上正在发生的事情，实际上主要围绕加密货币。人们在区块链上做的绝大部分活动，都被看作是加密资产、加密交易等等，但最终我们会走到一个比这无聊得多的阶段。

turns.en: And there's parts of this happening already today. We see it in industries like payments, in a lot of other places, but we need to get there kind of step by step, right?
turns.zh: 而这个过程的一部分今天已经在发生了。我们在支付等行业，还有很多其他领域都看到了，但我们需要一步一步地走到那一步，对吧？

turns.en: And to do that, what we need is funds, whether it's ETFs, mutual funds, what have you, to be represented on those blockchains so that you can move them around like you would a crypto asset.
turns.zh: 要做到这一点，我们需要的是让基金——不管是 ETF、共同基金还是别的什么——在那些区块链上被表示出来，这样你就能像转移加密资产一样去转移它们。

turns.en: And that's ultimately where we need to go, but we got quite a few steps to get there and the regulation is a big part of that. So this regulation right now has in essence opened up a window to allow this kind of product technology or innovation to enter the US markets in a kind of more controlled fashion.
turns.zh: 而这最终才是我们要去的方向，但我们还有好几步要走，而监管是其中很大的一块。所以眼下的这项监管，本质上是打开了一扇窗口，让这类产品技术或创新能够以一种相对可控的方式进入美国市场。

turns.en: Janice Henderson already has portfolio products that are so-called on-chain or tokenized. What exactly does that mean and how exactly does it differ, a tokenized fund, an ETF versus the ETF itself that you would trade anywhere like on Fidelity, Schwab or whatever platform you're on?
turns.zh: Janus Henderson 已经有了所谓链上（on-chain）或代币化的投资组合产品。那具体意味着什么？一个代币化的基金、代币化的 ETF，和你在任何地方——比如 Fidelity、Schwab，或者你所用的任何平台上——交易的那只 ETF 本身，到底有什么区别？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean this is the reason that this kind of step from the SEC is really important because today, right, we have about $50 billion worth of ETFs globally and they are accessed and distributed through the sort of traditional channels that people would expect, whether that's their wealth manager through a brokerage platform, etc.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说，这正是 SEC 迈出的这一步之所以真正重要的原因。因为今天，我们全球大概有 500 亿美元的 ETF，它们是通过人们习以为常的传统渠道被获取和分销的，不管是通过财富经理经由券商平台，等等。

turns.en: And then what we're doing in tokenization is really isolated from that. It's a separate universe of investors and we operate entirely offshore today because we don't have the regulatory clarity and some of the infrastructure pieces to make it possible for us to do it really at scale within the US.
turns.zh: 而我们在代币化上做的事情，实际上和那套体系是隔离开的。那是一个独立的投资者群体，而且我们今天完全在离岸运营，因为我们还没有足够的监管清晰度，也缺少一些基础设施，无法真正在美国境内大规模地做这件事。

turns.en: But right now we have sort of very similar funds, similar strategies that we manage for institutional investors who want to operate on-chain, who want to be able to integrate these types of solutions, these kind of investment opportunities into their portfolio alongside the other sort of crypto assets, decentralized finance, there's a sort of a range of reasons that people are using these things.
turns.zh: 但眼下我们管理着一些非常相似的基金、相似的策略，服务对象是那些想在链上运作、想把这类方案、这类投资机会和其他加密资产、去中心化金融（DeFi）一起纳入自己投资组合的机构投资者——人们使用这些东西的原因有很多方面。

turns.en: But this is a step to us bringing that closer to sort of that traditional model that we would expect an individual investor, for example, in the United States to be able to access through Schwab or Fidelity or whatever their brokerage platform is.
turns.zh: 但对我们来说，这一步是把它拉近到我们预期的那种传统模式，让美国这样的个人投资者能够通过 Schwab 或 Fidelity，或他们所用的任何券商平台去获得。

turns.en: But this is sort of a step in that direction still. Gabor, it's an interesting point that was brought up here with regard to kind of the similarities and maybe some of the subtle differences.
turns.zh: 但这仍然只是朝那个方向迈出的一步。Gabor，这里提到的关于相似之处、以及也许一些微妙差异的一点非常有意思。

turns.en: I wonder if you could take us through what exactly it looks like from a big picture standpoint and we'll drill down further, but from a big picture standpoint, what it means to be invested in a fund or a portfolio of assets that are put in an ETF wrapper right now, as opposed to owning units in that same fund that are then maybe put onto a chain, a blockchain somewhere that shows you what that ownership is, who had it and when the transaction occurred.
turns.zh: 我想请你从整体大局的角度带我们走一遍，我们再往细里挖。但从大局来看，投资于一支被装进 ETF 外壳的基金或资产组合，和持有同一支基金的份额、而这些份额随后被放到某个区块链上、链上记录显示你的所有权归谁、以及交易何时发生——这两者到底有什么区别？

turns.en: Yeah, so just if you want to think about tokenized assets, it's basically the same story as the ETF, put a little bit more evolution on infrastructure side.
turns.zh: 是的，如果你想理解代币化资产，它基本上和 ETF 是同一个故事，只是在基础设施层面多做了一点演进。

turns.en: So it's better, faster and cheaper. It's the next wrapper after ETFs. But it's also changing the fundamental structure in what I call the post ETF world.
turns.zh: 所以它更好、更快、更便宜。它是 ETF 之后的下一代外壳（wrapper）。但它也在改变我所说的那个后 ETF 时代（post-ETF world）的根本结构。

turns.en: So today, you go through around nine different intermediaries when you hit that buy button on Fidelity, Vanguard, Interactive Brokers or whatever until you own a stock.
turns.zh: 所以今天，当你在 Fidelity、Vanguard、Interactive Brokers 或任何平台按下买入键，到你真正持有一只股票，中间要经过大约九个不同的中介环节。

turns.en: The new SEC regulation basically says that if you are a RAGNMS stock, you can now structure it in a token format and sell it on the US markets. It could be stocks, it could be bundled stocks like ETFs and securities that you trade today.
turns.zh: 新的 SEC 监管规定基本上是说，如果你是一只符合 NMS 的股票，你现在可以把它构造成代币形式，并在美国市场上出售。它可以是股票，也可以是像 ETF 这样打包的股票，以及你今天交易的各类证券。

turns.en: So simultaneously, transfer agent laws and rules have also changed. So now you can record ownership and ownership records similarly to what you do in the traditional finance world.
turns.zh: 与此同时，过户代理（transfer agent）相关的法律和规则也改变了。所以现在你可以像在传统金融世界那样去记录所有权和所有权记录。

turns.en: So the experience will be very similar except you'll be able to hold your security on your phone and you can also settle it much faster and the tokenization will be basically allowing us to zero settlements, which is not here today. But for all intents and purposes, the experience should be very similar. The underlying infrastructure and cost structure are changing fundamentally. So we expect actually a tenfold reduction in cost because of the organization
turns.zh: 所以体验会非常相似，只不过你能把证券握在自己的手机里，而且你能更快完成结算，代币化基本上会让我们实现零时结算（zero settlement），这在今天是做不到的。但就所有实际目的而言，体验应该非常相似。底层的基础设施和成本结构正在发生根本性改变。所以实际上我们预期成本会降十倍——由于组织和

turns.en: and infrastructure change and basically a reduction of six to seven intermediaries from the current system of nine. But the experience shouldn't change that much.
turns.zh: 基础设施的改变，并且基本上从当前九个中介的系统里减少六到七个中介。但体验不会有太大变化。

turns.en: How, Gabor, could I follow up there? You laid out some of the maybe similarities and subtle differences, but how exactly does that experience change given the fact that something is on chain versus not on a chain? You mentioned all the counterparties that are involved in the transaction of an ETF. What exactly will be similar and different, again, big strokes wise in just buying my ETF and portfolio units in my traditional route versus on chain? Why exactly is on chain
turns.zh: Gabor，我能接着问一下吗？你刚才讲到了一些相似之处和微妙差异，但考虑到有些东西在链上、有些不在链上，这个体验具体会怎么改变？你提到了 ETF 交易中涉及的各个交易对手方。那么，通过传统路径买入我的 ETF 和组合份额，与在链上买入，到底哪里相同、哪里不同——先从大框架上说？链上为什么

turns.en: going to be the future besides the fact that you mentioned cost could be significantly less? Yeah, so again, the rule changes on transfer agencies particularly are important. So who records the ownership is changing? So it might not be the DTC. It might not be your fund administrator or custodian, but you will be able to transfer agents. These new type of transfer agents like OpenAgent will be able to basically transfer ownership more efficiently. But the
turns.zh: 会成为未来，除了你提到的成本可能大幅降低之外？是的，那再说一遍，过户代理方面的规则变化尤其重要。所以，谁来记录所有权这一点正在改变。可能就不再是 DTC 了，可能也不是你的基金管理人或托管人，而是过户代理。像 OpenAgent 这类新型的过户代理，将能够更高效地转移所有权。但是

turns.en: experience, again, should be very similar. It is the plumbing for large institutions that will change. The end user experience will be relatively similar. Again, just the system will be more efficient. The on chain pieces of it is I think crypto did a good job showing that distribution is possible into more retail user bases and untouched parts of the world. So currently about 89% of the world does not have access to a brokerage account. So issuers, ETF powerhouses, managers,
turns.zh: 体验，再说一遍，应该非常相似。真正改变的是大型机构背后的那套管道。终端用户的体验会相对相似。只是系统会更高效。链上的这一部分——我认为加密货币很好地证明了，分销是可以触达更多零售用户群体、以及世界上那些原本被忽略的角落的。目前全球大约 89% 的人还没有券商账户的渠道。所以发行人、ETF 巨头、管理人、

turns.en: and even stock and bond issuers will be able to distribute their products more broadly. But again, for the end double markets like in the US where brokerage participation is pretty high, the experience will be similar. Nick, one of the interesting parts about this conversation as well is just how I guess forcefully and how I guess maybe I guess the right term is to maybe say how quickly will people adopt this kind of technology? There's a reason why there are
turns.zh: 甚至股票和债券发行人，都将能更广泛地分销他们的产品。但话说回来，对于像美国这样券商参与度很高的终端市场，体验会相似。Nick，这场对话里有个很有意思的部分，就是——我想该用什么词——人们到底会多快、或者多坚决地采用这类技术？之所以有这样的差别，是因为

turns.en: some folks out there offshore to the United States who are a lot more active in these types of markets with regard to tokenized assets on a blockchain somewhere. When you roll out hypothetically or any other issuer does in the United States, fund link products that are then tokenized and put on a chain somewhere, how quickly do you feel as though you will have to deal with the adoption?
turns.zh: 在美国之外的离岸地区，有些人在区块链上这类代币化资产市场中要活跃得多。当你——或者假设任何一家发行人在美国——推出发行、然后被代币化并放到某个链上的基金产品时，你觉得自己在应对采用（adoption）这件事上会有多快？

turns.en: Is it going to be a ramp up relatively quickly or do you think it'll take years before people really start to feel as though they have the comfort level to transact in tokenized products that are on a chain somewhere that are not necessarily something they can go to their online account and see this is, I hold 100 shares of some Janice Henderson fund.
turns.zh: 是会比较快地爬坡上升，还是你觉得要好几年人们才会真正感到有足够的安全感，去交易那些放在某个链上的代币化产品——那些东西未必是他们能登录自己的线上账户、然后看到「我持有 100 股某支 Janus Henderson 基金」的？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, I started in ETFs almost 25 years ago and at that time we were out talking to investors about what the benefits were of ETFs and why they should consider using them. And I think they were quite clear. There was very material advantages to investors in many cases to use an ETF over traditional fund wrapper and yet 25 years later we're still having that conversation.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说，我进入 ETF 这个行业差不多已经 25 年了。那时候我们就在外面跟投资者讲 ETF 的好处是什么、他们为什么该考虑用它。我觉得那些好处是很清楚的。在很多情况下，相比传统基金外壳，用 ETF 对投资者有实实在在的重大优势，可 25 年过去了，我们还在进行同样的对话。

turns.en: And so I think the adoption will be faster here just because of the nature of the technology. And so just purely cost is not going to be enough. I think if you said the only benefit of having these types of wrappers move on chain versus a traditional brokerage model was going to be cost savings, I just don't think it would be enough because to your point the U.S.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这一次的采用会更快，仅仅是因为这项技术的性质。光靠成本本身是不够的。我觉得如果你说把这类外壳搬到链上、相比传统券商模式的唯一好处就是省钱，我觉得那还不够，因为正如你所说，美国

turns.en: market is pretty efficient. So there's costs that we can cut out. There's a lot of intermediaries. Let's simplify it. Let's make it better for investors and we certainly think that's going to happen. But as you go offshore, maybe it's much, much more inefficient and so there's a lot more savings to be had there. So I think what you're going to have to see is adoption offshore to really crystallize this, create a market, create some dynamics and then onshore
turns.zh: 市场已经相当高效了。所以有些成本我们确实能砍掉。有很多中介，让我们把它简化、让它对投资者更友好，我们当然认为这会发生。但到了离岸市场，那里的低效可能要严重得多，所以那里的节省空间也大得多。所以我认为你会看到的是：先靠离岸的采用把它真正沉淀下来，形成一个市场、形成一些动能，然后回到美国境内

turns.en: it's going to take a little bit more than cost. And I think one of the things that is really critical is unlocking new things that you can do. So if you think about ETFs, the fact that I can hold an ETF in a brokerage account, what's one of the things that made possible for investors that they couldn't really do in a mutual fund? Well, it was shorting. Before the advent of the ETF, the idea of individual investor, even a very high net worth investor, being able to go short
turns.zh: 它需要的就不仅仅是成本优势了。我觉得真正关键的一点，是解锁一些你以前做不到的新事情。想想 ETF：我能在一个券商账户里持有 ETF，这一点让投资者能做到、而在共同基金里其实做不到的事情是什么？是做空（shorting）。在 ETF 出现之前，一个个人投资者，就算是非常高净值的投资者，想要去做空

turns.en: an actively managed portfolio or a diversified fund, it was virtually impossible. And now it's just normal, right? I can buy options. I can short. There's all of this infrastructure that's now deployed against ETFs that wasn't possible in traditional fund wrappers. Well, there's another evolution of that which is coming with blockchain. And so there's this idea that I can sort of custody my assets in my wallet and now I can do all sorts of things across barriers that today exist in
turns.zh: 一支主动管理的组合或一支分散化的基金，几乎是不可能的。而现在这稀松平常，对吧？我能买期权，我能做空，现在有整套基础设施都是围绕 ETF 部署的，这在传统基金外壳里根本不可能。而区块链会带来这套演进的下一个版本。所以有这么一个概念：我可以在自己的钱包里托管资产，然后我就能跨越传统金融市场

turns.en: traditional financial markets. So even just simple things, if I think about my bank account and maybe I need to have a checking account and a savings account to get a little bit higher yield and then I need some assets in a money market fund and then I need to be able to wire money, all of that can be collapsed, right? And in addition, I can now start thinking about other assets that can come in there.
turns.zh: 如今存在的种种壁垒去做各种各样的事情。就算是很简单的事，想想我的银行账户——也许我需要一个支票账户、一个储蓄账户才能拿到稍微高一点的收益，然后我需要一些资产放在货币市场基金里，然后我还得能电汇——所有这些都能被折叠合一，对吧？而且除此之外，我可以开始设想其他各种资产也能进到那里。

turns.en: So in some future state, what if I want to pay my rent with my S&P 500, right? Today that's just impossible. But this utility, this increased ability to make your assets, your investment assets deliver more value to you, I think is really what's going to drive that adoption. And so I understand Gabor's point that it should be kind of seamless. And so that is true. We can replicate the existing brokerage model on chain and have an investor not really see anything different.
turns.zh: 所以在某种未来的状态下，假如我想用我的标普 500（S&P 500）敞口来付房租呢？今天这根本不可能。但这种效用、这种让你的资产、让你的投资资产为你带来更多价值的能力的提升，我认为才是真正驱动采用的东西。所以我理解 Gabor 说的——它应该几乎是无缝的。这没错。我们可以在链上复刻现有的券商模式，让投资者几乎看不出任何不同。

turns.en: But I actually think what will happen is whole new business models will evolve. And we're seeing this already in, for example, crypto exchanges who've pioneered whole new ways to trade crypto assets offshore largely. But that can come onshore, right? And it's going to touch a lot of different parts of the financial market. And I think that's why the SEC is doing what they're doing, which we certainly applaud around this innovation exemption is, well,
turns.zh: 但我其实认为，会发生的是全新的商业模式会演化出来。我们已经看到这一点，比如在加密货币交易所——它们开创了全新的交易加密资产的方式，主要在离岸。但这些东西可以回到境内，对吧？它会触及金融市场的很多不同部分。我想这也是 SEC 在做他们正在做的事情的原因——我们对这项创新豁免（innovation exemption）当然是赞赏的——那就是：

turns.en: let's start. Let's start the process. Let's get people experimenting. Let's test the system. But ultimately, I think it's more than just cost. There's really changes in the fundamental way in which financial services can be delivered. How much, Gabor? I'll ask this to you because it was brought up, and Nick just brought it up, this idea that there are seamless aspects to this.
turns.zh: 让我们开始吧。让我们启动这个过程。让人们去试验，去测试这套系统。但最终，我认为它不仅仅是成本。金融服务交付方式的根本层面正在改变。Gabor，我要把这个问题问你，因为这个话题被提起了，Nick 刚才也提到了这种无缝的说法。

turns.en: It also, by the way, necessitates a comfort level with a kind of technology that is not inherent to financial markets in the US at least right now. But that could be in the future. How much are people going to look at this and say, I need extra security? Nick mentioned, could I have it in my own digital wallet? Is that kind of detached from other networks, or is it kind of like in a cold storage capacity? Or if it's something you access on your phone

And then we see then eventually the benefit that they're deriving

turns.en: to be able to come back. And so, I think that we'll see that transition to our traditional clients, but it's just going to take a little bit of time. All right. turns.zh: 能够回流。所以我想我们会看到这种向传统客户的过渡，只是需要一点时间。好，这确实是一场引人入胜的对话。我真希望我们有大把时间，因为这显然是很多人心目中的一个大话题。现在，我们要用节目里「市场 102」（Markets 102）这一段，通过一些深入分析和视角，来为这场对话收尾，帮你更好地理解 ETF。

turns.en: Gabor Gorbach, Open Assets founder and CEO, continues with us. Now, Gabor, thanks for sticking around for our podcast. I want to kind of build on some of the stuff that we talked about during the ETF Ed Show this week, which is to identify some of the ways that tokenization, especially when it comes to the fund management business, how exactly will tokenization make things that much better and or at the very least different than the experience that we have right
turns.zh: Open Assets 创始人兼首席执行官 Gabor Gurbacs 继续和我们在一起。Gabor，谢谢你留下来上我们的节目。我想接着本周在 ETF Edge 节目里聊到的一些话题往下走，也就是找出代币化——尤其在基金管理业务上——究竟会在哪些方面让事情变得更好，或者至少让体验与我们此刻所拥有的有所不同，而我们又

turns.en: now? And are there certain parts of the fund management and distribution chain that will be more disrupted by putting things on chain, so to speak? Tokenization is the better, faster, cheaper story that we have seen in technology for a long time. So that's what's happening now to the financial services industry that for all intents and purposes hasn't changed for 50 years. The parts of it that is changing is the settlement piece of it and the middle part of
turns.zh: 现在所处的体验到底有什么不同？基金管理链条和分销链条里，是不是有些部分会因为把东西放上链而受到更大的冲击？代币化就是我们长期以来在技术上看到的那个「更好、更快、更便宜」的故事。所以现在这一切正降临到那个其实五十年来几乎没怎么变过的金融服务行业。正在改变的那部分，是其中的结算环节，以及

turns.en: butter the stack, the issuance piece of it, not so much in trading, not so much. What I believe is important is that currently, once you hit buy on a stock, on a brokerage, whether it's Fidelity, Vanguard, Schwab, Interactive Brokers, or you name it, Robinhood, your order goes through a chain of nine to 10 different country parties and you don't actually end up owning something a day or two later depending on what you buy. So tokenization helps you
turns.zh: 整个技术栈中间那一层，也就是发行环节；交易这一侧的改变没那么多。我认为重要的是：目前，当你在券商那里对一只股票按下买入——不管是 Fidelity、Vanguard、Schwab、Interactive Brokers，还是你说得出的任何一家，Robinhood——你的订单要经过九到十个不同交易对手方组成的一条链，而实际上你是一两天之后才真正拥有你买的东西，取决于你买的是什么。所以代币化帮你

turns.en: basically to do that instantly and replace the current chain of intermediaries that is about nine to about three. So fund administrators, central depositories, transfer agents, and custodians perform functions that will merge into very likely one entity and most of it will be performed by the transfer agent. Exchanges will not change so much. The role of the asset architect or the issuer will not change so much, but the back end sort of settlement that will change a lot.
turns.zh: 基本上做到即时完成，并把当前这条中介链从大约九个压缩到大约三个。所以基金管理人、中央存管机构、过户代理和托管人，它们履行的职能很可能会合并成一个实体，而其中大部分将由过户代理来执行。交易所的变化不会那么大。资产设计者或发行人的角色变化也不会那么大，但后端的结算会大幅改变。

turns.en: So I'll stop there because I think the big important portion of all this is technology is making intermediaries less relevant. And today, again, it's a hodgepodge of coupled together tech from 50 years ago by nine to 10 different intermediaries performing functions that blockchains can do it for really 10 to 30x more efficiently from a price perspective and way, way faster. So that's what's replacing the current tech stack.
turns.zh: 所以我就说到这儿，因为我认为这一切里最重要的部分是：技术正在让中介变得没那么不可或缺。今天，再说一遍，它是五十年的、由九到十个不同中介拼凑在一起的一套杂乱技术，各自履行着一些功能；而区块链能以价格上 10 到 30 倍的效率、快得多的速度把这些功能做掉。所以这就是在替换当前的技术栈。

turns.en: So does it stand to reason then, Gabor, that we will not call it, say, hypothetically in 10, 15, 20, 30 years, have any of the same types of institutions or intermediaries that they will all be replaced by blockchain technology and the use of tokenized assets and securities that are on chain somewhere? In other words, is it fair to say or not fair to say that the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ will not be around in 10 to 20 years? Is it fair to say that brokerages,
turns.zh: 那么 Gabor，是不是可以这样推断：假设在 10 年、15 年、20 年、30 年后，我们不会再有今天这些同类的机构或中介，它们都会被区块链技术和放在某个链上的代币化资产、证券所取代？换句话说，说纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克在 10 到 20 年后将不复存在，这个说法公道还是不公道？说券商，

turns.en: as we know them today, like the list that you mentioned, will not be around because things are done on different types of platforms than they are right now?
turns.zh: 像我们今天所认识的那样、像你提到的那份清单那样，将不复存在，因为事情会在不同类型的平台上完成，而不是像现在这样——这种说法对吗？

turns.en: I think the NASDAQs and New York Stock exchanges of the world will be around. They are a place for price discovery and price formation. So I think trading is pretty efficient and it will be around.
turns.zh: 我认为纳斯达克和纽约证券交易所这些机构会留下来。它们是价格发现和定价形成的场所。所以我认为交易这一侧是相对高效的，它会留下来。

turns.en: But the settlement piece of fund administrators, custodians in this current form, central depositories, they may not be around unless they vote because, again, blockchains and automated administrative functions literally perform six to seven different intermediaries rule automatically and very cost efficiently. So there might be administering some of the functions for blockchains, but they will certainly not perform the services in their current forms.
turns.zh: 但基金管理人、托管人以目前形态存在的结算环节、中央存管机构，它们可能不会留下来——除非它们进化——因为区块链和自动化的管理职能，实际上是把六到七个不同中介的职责自动、并以极低的成本完成了。所以也许还会为一些区块链执行部分管理职能，但它们肯定不会再以目前的形态提供这些服务。

turns.en: And I do think, yes, this new infrastructure does kill two thirds of the financial infrastructure stuck for the better because a lot of these entities are not adding much value. They are extremely costly and they are intermediating processes for no good reason. And so they will have to either evolve or they will be out of business. But it will be mostly the settlement and the administration of the assets. It will not be the places for trading and it will not be the
turns.zh: 我确实认为，是的，这套新基础设施会消灭掉金融基础设施的三分之二——而且是好事，因为其中很多实体并没有创造多少价值。它们成本极高，毫无道理地在为各种流程做中间人。所以它们要么进化，要么退出市场。但这主要集中在结算和资产管理这一侧，不会是交易场所，也不会是

turns.en: asset architects and issuers. If those things are going to be fairly static and can evolve with speed on chain, what then is going to be the kind of takeaway for people who use or want to use this
turns.zh: 资产设计者和发行人。那么如果情况是这样，如果交易本身已经很高效、也许只能边际上更高效一点，因为它现在已经非常高效了；那些价格发现工具，也就是让你看到什么交易、以什么价格、在什么时间发生的东西——如果这些都将基本保持静态、而在链上又能快速演进，那么对于使用、或想使用

turns.en: kind of technology? It seems to me then, if it's not price discovery and it's not the trading that are ultimately going to be disrupted, it is the ledger aspect that provides the real value, right? The understanding that you have somewhere on chain that tells you that I hypothetically own this asset and transacted it at a certain time and place and it tells me somewhere in a distributed ledger format that I'm the one who actually has ownership of said asset, right?
turns.zh: 这类技术的人来说，真正的收获会是什么？在我看来，如果最终被颠覆的不是价格发现、也不是交易，那么真正提供价值的是账本（ledger）那一面，对吧？那种认知——你在链上某个地方有一张记录，告诉我我名义上拥有这项资产、在某个时间地点成交了，并以分布式账本的形式告诉我，我才是那个真正拥有那项资产所有权的人，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah, so again, I think there's their new transfer agent rules. So transfer agents are evolving and I don't think transfer agents will go away. So you'll have legal holders of record and places of ownership to transfer agent that uses a blockchain to track ownership. So you'll see that the ownership records will just be published by the transfer agent. So that's what will happen. And for the end user, there's no change in experience from a brokerage perspective,
turns.zh: 是的，再说一遍，我认为会有新的过户代理规则。所以过户代理在演进，我不认为过户代理会消失。你会有合法的登记持有人（holder of record），会有使用区块链来追踪所有权的过户代理。所以你会看到所有权记录将由过户代理来发布，这就是会发生的事。而对终端用户来说，从券商角度体验没有变化，

turns.en: but the value chain behind it will be so much more efficient that when you buy something on a brokerage platform, you actually own it immediately. And currently, it's basically pretend ownership until a day or two later. Cash is not fast enough and securities are not fast enough for you to own it. So if there's a financial crisis during that day, when you bought a security, very likely your account will blow up. And so those types of scenarios
turns.zh: 但它背后的价值链会高效得多，以至于当你在一个券商平台上买某样东西时，你立刻就真正拥有了它。而目前基本上是一种「假装拥有」，要等一两天之后才成真。现金不够快，证券也不够快，你还没真正拥有它。所以如果在你买入证券的当天爆发了金融危机，你的账户很可能是会爆掉的。而这类情形

turns.en: are avoided with this new technology. You will also have ownership rights to the actual security versus a lot of the times you basically get versions of promissory notes from various institutions that may or may not even back your securities with real assets. A lot of custodians have very little insurance behind securities. I've seen $10 billion funds being backed by $10 million bonds. And so those are if those institutions go down, you don't have even,
turns.zh: 用这项新技术就能避免。你还将对真正的证券拥有所有权，而很多时候你拿到的其实是一版版本票（promissory note），来自各种机构，它们或许会用真实资产来支撑你的证券，或许不会。很多托管人在证券背后几乎没什么保险。我见过 100 亿美元的基金只被 1000 万美元的债券所支撑。而如果这些机构倒了，你甚至

turns.en: record of ownership, can't prove it because you see eight layers of promissory bonds over promissory bonds versus direct ownership, which is where we are getting. But the vast majority of the world doesn't even have access to brokerage. And they're not going to replicate the current hodgepodge, centrally cleared infrastructure. 89% of the world
turns.zh: 都没有所有权记录，无法证明，因为你看到的是本票套本票、一层层叠了八层，而不是直接拥有——而我们正在走向的就是直接拥有。再说一遍，我们很幸运，在 G7、也许 G20 国家，我们有渠道用到还算不错的券商，体验也够好。但世界上绝大多数人甚至接触不到券商。而他们也不会去复制眼下这套杂乱的、中央清算的基础设施。全球 89% 的人

turns.zh: 接触不到券商。对我们来说这听起来很疯狂，因为我们肯定有三四个不同的券商账户，但现实就是这样。而人们不谈的另一面是：今天，要让某样东西进到公开市场、去上市，实在太难了。

The reason why you can't do that is because the super intermediate infrastructure makes it so expensive that entrepreneurs can't access the public market. That's why it's this way, which seems just crazy because if you travel anywhere in Asia, for instance, you are able to raise money on various platforms. And like in the US, it's just, we're not there because the
turns.zh: 负担太重了。作为公司，你不能直接跑到公开市场去融资。你不能这么做的原因是，那套超级中介的基础设施让成本高昂到创业者根本进不了公开市场。所以才会是这个样子，而这在我看来简直疯狂。因为如果你在亚洲任何地方走走，比如，你就能在各种平台上融资。而在美国，我们之所以做不到，是因为

turns.en: underlying infrastructure is actually inhibiting. So what I expect is there's going to be a lot more companies with tokenization that can go public, the public markets will flourish a lot.
turns.zh: 底层基础设施实际上在起阻碍作用。所以我预期的是，会因为代币化出现多得多的公司能够上市，公开市场会繁荣得多。

turns.en: You'll see many IPOs and IPO sizes reducing a lot. So in emerging markets, we see between five and 25 million IPO type of tokenized security issuances, and those markets are flourishing. So entrepreneurs can raise capital directly on public markets. That just doesn't exist in the US. And this also means just a much bigger point that returns are not democratized, like it's venture capital, private equity, and select very few people and companies that can
turns.zh: 你会看到 IPO 数量增多、而 IPO 的规模大幅缩小。所以在新兴市场，我们看到 500 万到 2500 万美元这种量级的代币化证券发行，那些市场正在繁荣。所以创业者可以直接在公开市场融资。而这在美国根本不存在。这也意味着一个更大的要点：回报并没有被民主化。就像风险投资、私募股权，只有极少数人和公司能够

turns.en: access growth stories. And with this new technology, we can open it up to more people. And that's the goal of regulators too, and that will help capital formation, that will help public markets grow, and that will help the distribution of assets as well more broadly in the US.
turns.zh: 接触到成长型的故事。而有了这项新技术，我们可以把它向更多人敞开。这也是监管者的目标，这会帮助资本形成，会帮助公开市场成长，也会帮助资产在美国更广泛地分配。

turns.en: And one final question before we let you go here. Given the fact that we have this kind of relative clarity with regard to kind of regulatory activity around tokenization, knowing what we know right now, what are your expectations for the adoption of tokenization over the course of the next one, three, five years?
turns.zh: 在你离开之前，还有最后一个问题。既然我们现在围绕代币化的监管活动有了这种相对的清晰度，就我们目前所知，你对未来 1 年、3 年、5 年内代币化的采用有什么预期？

So it's all happening very fast. So I think 10% of assets will be tokenized within the next three years. And again, a lot of the change will also happen fast. So we can switch away trillions of dollars in assets from the current infrastructure
turns.zh: 是的，我想，你看，现在在美国，股票市场大概 69 到 70 万亿，债券市场 60 万亿，全球资产需求 320 万亿，我想我们大概会在两三年内达到 10% 的资产被代币化。所以这一切发生得很快。所以我认为 10% 的资产会在未来三年内被代币化。而同样，很多改变也会很快发生。所以我们可以从当前的基础设施上切换掉数万亿美元的资产——

So I think my expectation is 10% of all assets will be tokenized roughly within the next three, five years, let me say three, five. And we'll see, I mean, we're already seeing asset managers racing into the space very quickly and trying to issue their assets to get in front of very successful user bases. Everyone looks at the coin bases,
turns.zh: 只要按一下按钮，如果洲际交易所（Intercontinental Exchange）决定这么做，或者如果 DTCC 决定完成现代化改造并这么做。所以我的预期是，大概 10% 的资产会在未来三到五年内被代币化，让我说三年、五年。我们会看到——我是说，我们已经看到资产管理人非常快地涌入这个领域，设法发行他们的资产，去抢先触达那些非常成功的用户群体。人人都盯着 Coinbase，

turns.en: crackings and tethers of the world. How do you manage to get hundreds of millions of users and people want to sell into those channels? So they have to communicate and wrap assets, the asset managers into a format that a new generation users use, which is will be true tokenization. So I think the change will be fast. And you know, there's a third of the world's population is under 19 years of age, another third of the population, the world's population is under 34.
turns.zh: Kraken 和 Tether 这些公司。它们是怎么做到获得数亿用户的，人们都想进入那些渠道去销售。所以资产管理者必须把资产用格式化的方式，包装成新一代用户所使用的形式，那才是真正的代币化。所以我认为改变会很快。你看，全球三分之一的人口在 19 岁以下，还有三分之一的世界人口在 34 岁以下。

turns.en: So every like, roughly between 13 to 17 years, there is a paradigm shift and things happen very quickly. We're basically 10 years into the next paradigm change within the next five to seven years, we'll have a large amount of young people with a lot of disposable income using assets very differently. And you know, the 20 year olds of the world don't think about what a growth or value of ETF is, they buy crypto in an exchange. And so that will be,
turns.zh: 所以大概每 13 到 17 年，就会有一次范式转移，很多事情会很快发生。我们基本上处在下一次范式变革的头 10 年里；未来五到七年，会有大量拥有很多可支配收入的年轻人，用完全不同的方式使用资产。而 20 岁的年轻人不会去想一支 ETF 的成长或价值是什么，他们在交易所买加密货币。所以那将会——
